label: S. 3971

selection.reason: Impact scored and summarised by Gemini.

summary: The Small Business Innovation and Economic Security Act reauthorizes and updates the Small Business Innovation Research (SBIR) program, the Small Business Technology Transfer (STTR) program, and related pilot programs through fiscal year 2031. It strengthens security risk evaluations for award applicants, creates strategic breakthrough funding for critical technologies with matching funds, sets limits on the number of proposals small businesses can submit to reduce administrative burdens, improves Phase III commercialization training and support, and enhances data collection and tracking systems for awards.

affected_groups.effect: Must undergo enhanced security risk and foreign ownership evaluations, face limits on proposal submissions per fiscal year, but gain access to larger strategic breakthrough funding, expanded TABA uses, and simplified Phase III contracting.
affected_groups.group: Small businesses applying for or receiving SBIR and STTR awards

affected_groups.effect: Must conduct rigorous security and watchlist checks, set and enforce proposal limits, provide justifications and notices for security-related denials, train their contracting workforces on Phase III awards, and update tracking systems.
affected_groups.group: Federal agencies administering SBIR and STTR programs

key_provisions: Reauthorizes through September 30, 2031, the SBIR and STTR programs as well as multiple associated pilot programs.
Expands federal agency requirements to evaluate security risks, foreign ownership, and connections to entities listed on specific restricted trade, military, or security watchlists.
Establishes strategic breakthrough allocations of up to $30,000,000 for Phase II awards to small businesses meeting critical technology needs with at least 100 percent matching funds.
Directs federal program office directors to establish equal limits on the maximum number of proposals a small business can submit in a fiscal year, with narrow waiver exceptions.
Improves technical and business assistance (TABA) options, allowing awardees to use funds for staff hiring, training, cybersecurity, foreign involvement screening, and I-Corps participation.
Enhances training for agency contracting officers and acquisition workforces regarding Phase III commercialization, data rights, and sole-source contracts.
Updates federal databases and procurement data systems to track specific award categories such as direct-to-Phase II, strategic breakthrough awards, and Phase III contracts.
missing_information: Exact quantitative estimates of the number of small businesses that will be impacted or denied awards due to new security rules.
Specific details on the exact proposal limits each agency will establish, as those are delegated to individual program office directors.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The Small Business Innovation and Economic Security Act reauthorizes and updates the Small Business Innovation Research (SBIR) program, the Small Business Technology Transfer (STTR) program, and related pilot programs through fiscal year 2031. It strengthens security risk evaluations for award applicants, creates strategic breakthrough funding for critical technologies with matching funds, sets limits on the number of proposals small businesses can submit to reduce administrative burdens, improves Phase III commercialization training and support, and enhances data collection and tracking systems for awards.
summary_detail.significance: This legislation affects the operations and research funding of domestic small businesses engaged in federal research and development, while significantly increasing national security scrutiny and inter-agency coordination regarding foreign risks and supply chain threats.
